title: latency-cartography-scratch-gabriel
body:
Purpose:
Quick field notebook: map out how latency percentiles change across three axes I care about for small (seq<=128) text-gen workloads: cache hit rate (0-100%), concurrent QPS (10-1000), and batch coalescing window (0-25ms). Goal is a practical map I can reference when recommending default batch/window settings for Hosted API tiers.

Testbed:
- Model: mix of Llama-2-13B-ish variant (quantized INT8 runtime), local staging cluster (dedicated single GPU node for each worker)
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-40GB equivalent (staging lab), 8 worker pods behind ingress proxy
- Runtime: rwd-runtime:main@2025-09 (local build with continuous-batching changes + KV cache TTL adjust)
- Workload generator: custom python harness (arrival patterns: Poisson, clustered bursts, deterministic ramp), token lengths sampled from production token histogram (median 56, 95th 120)
- Metric collection: Prometheus counters (request_latency_seconds.{p50,p95,p99}), per-model kv_cache_hit_rate gauge, tx/s throughput, queuing_time histograms

Experiment matrix (high-level):
- Cache hit rate sweep: 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 95% (simulated by prefix-cache lookup probability)
- QPS sweep: 25, 100, 250, 500, 1000
- Batch window: 0ms (no coalesce), 3ms, 8ms, 20ms
- Arrival pattern: steady Poisson vs bursty (sine-wave envelope with 2s period, peak-to-base 6x)
- Each cell: 2 x 3m runs (stabilize 30s, measure 150s), keep seeds for harness

Representative raw observations:
- Baseline (0% cache, QPS 100, window 8ms, Poisson): p50=42ms, p95=182ms, p99=412ms, throughput ~96rps (drop due to internal queuing backpressure).
- With 75% cache hit at same QPS/window: p50=31ms, p95=95ms, p99=160ms, throughput ~99rps. Major reduction in tail.
- High concurrency (QPS 500, 0% cache, window 8ms, Poisson): p50=55ms, p95=430ms, p99=980ms; observed amplification in p95->p99 as queuing/backpressure kicks in.
- Burst case (QPS envelope peak 600, avg ~150, 50% cache, window 8ms): transient p99 spikes up to 1.4s during peaks; p95 less extreme (~420ms).
- Mini-window (3ms) at QPS 250, 50% cache: lower p95 vs 8ms by ~12% but p50 ~same. At QPS 1000, reducing window to 3ms increased head-of-line contention and raised p99 by ~220ms relative to 8ms (too small window -> more small batches => more context switches).
- No-coalesce (0ms) consistently had worse p95/p99 at >250 QPS vs tuned windows; at very low QPS (<=25) 0ms avoids added latency cost of hold-and-wait and is slightly better.

Notes from charts (see linked grafana):
- Iso-latency contours (p95) look roughly hyperbolic in QPS x cache-hit space: to keep p95 < 200ms, you either need cache_hit>65% at 250 QPS or keep QPS<120 at cache_hit=25%.
- p99 surfaces show steeper cliffs (non-linear) when QPS crosses batch-size-saturation points. Those cliffs align with increases in observed batch sizes and corresponding kernel scheduling delays.

Quick heuristics (for product defaults):
- Hosted free tier (low qps, bursty): default window=3ms, disable heavy coalescing for <=50rps clients; fallback to 8ms if average session activity grows >200rps to amortize kernel startup.
- Standard tier: default window=8ms, aim for system-level cache hit >=50% via prefix caching suggestions, autoscale thresholds target keeping per-worker QPS < 300.
- Dedicated GPU pools: allow window up to 20ms for steady-high QPS workloads (>500rps) to maximize throughput; enforce tail SLO with smarter preemption when queue length > threshold.

Anomalies / gotchas observed:
1) KV cache hit sim approach: synthetic hits that skip full forward pass are slightly optimistic versus real workload because some code paths still touch small token prefix ops; measured 'true' production cache benefit likely ~0.9x of our sim.
2) At high QPS, small window sizes caused more inter-thread contention in runtime's batching queue (thread locking observed in perf top). Need to instrument lock hold times.
3) On burst edges, observed ~5-8% request drop (502 gateway timeout) due to ingress proxy queue limits before runtime backpressure engages — suggests we should increase proxy queue or tune ingress backoff.

Open questions / next probes:
- Validate cache simulation fidelity: run small controlled A/B against real cached workload (with deterministic prefixes) and compare per-stage CPU/GPU ops to isolate optimistic bits.
- Lock profiling: add eBPF sampler to capture mutex contention in coalescing queue at 3ms/8ms/20ms windows.
- Can runtime add jittered release (randomized small epsilon) to reduce synchronized microbursts when many connections start sessions simultaneously? Quick sim looked promising.
- How much do kernel launch amortizations change on different GPU types (A100 vs H100)? Need one quick cross-hardware run.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Push a short perf patch that logs batching queue lock hold time (Gabriel) — due by next sprint prep
- [ ] Run cache-fidelity A/B with Maya: 2026-03-03 (low priority, needs test data)
- [ ] Raise ingress proxy queue limit in staging and re-run burst envelopes to verify 502s elimination (Ibrahim)
- [ ] Draft a simple one-page recommendation for product defaults based on windows vs QPS vs cache-hit contours (deliverable for Hosted defaults)

Quick TL;DR for slack post:
Mapped p95/p99 across cache-hit x QPS x window. Main takeaway: cache-hit % has outsized benefit on tails; moderate batch windows (8ms) are sweet spot for most mid-QPS workloads; very small windows help low-QPS but backfire at very high QPS because of added contention. Need to fix ingress queue limits and profile lock hold times.

Raw snippets (copyable commands):
- harness run: python harness/run_sweep.py --model llama-13b-int8 --qps 250 --window_ms 8 --cache_hit 0.5 --pattern poisson --seed 42 --out /tmp/cartography/250_8_50.json
- prom query (p95 last 3m): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[3m])) by (le, instance))

Thoughts to keep: 'cartography' is useful as a visual language for product conversations. Next time: add an overlay of cost-per-token curves to see where tail improvements justify dedicated capacity.

End of scratch notes.
